content.caption: Case study diagram showing how a persistent Wiki Layer (skill-impact.md, logs.md, patterns) informs evolution of the break-repetition-loop skill in the Active Skill Layer on ALFWorld.
content.description: A two-panel diagram. The left panel, 'Persistent Wiki Layer (wiki/)', has three gray boxes. The first, skill-impact.md, records Iteration 0: create goal-directed-action, marked REJECTED, with a diff snippet adding goal-directed-action/SKILL.md. Below it, Iteration 1: create break-repetition-loop and Iteration 4: update break-repetition-loop are both marked ACCEPTED. The second box, logs.md, lists Iteration 0: create take-examine-move-loop.md (train: 00, 02) and reject skill 'goal-directed-action' (val score = 0.72). It then lists Iteration 1: errors re-occurring (train: 01, 02), Use-Examine Loop (NEW) in train: 30, 31, appending fresh evidence to take-examine-move-loop.md, and accepting skill 'break-repetition-loop' (val score = 0.78). The third box, patterns, contains take-examine-move-loop.md and multi-operation-loop.md, each with a description and evidence by iteration. The right panel, 'Active Skill Layer (skills/)', is a green box for break-repetition-loop. Its PURPOSE.md explains that the previous attempt goal-directed-action was rejected as too abstract. Its SKILL.md has a Trigger, two Rules with failing and successful examples, and an Anti-Pattern (Take -> Operate -> Move -> Take, an infinite cycle) with a Fix. A collapsed other-skill box sits below. Colored arrows connect the panels. A red arrow is labeled 'Prior Rejection History Explains Skill Rationale' and points to PURPOSE.md. A green arrow is labeled 'Accepted Proposed Skill Update' and points to SKILL.md. A blue arrow is labeled 'Evolution Log Chronologically Records Patterns and Decisions'. A yellow arrow is labeled 'Documented Patterns Motivate the Skill Update Proposals at Iterations 1 and 4' and points from patterns to the SKILL.md rules.
